Subject: Geofence waiver & subprocessor evidence

Connor —

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re close on the purchase order but legal has a couple of outstanding asks before procurement can sign:

1) Can you confirm whether our EU tenant can be pinned to EU-only processing, and if so, what your failover policy is for transient cross-border processing (e.g., during region outages)? Specifically we need to know the maximum duration and whether any customer data is written to non-EU subsystems.

2) We require an up-to-date subprocessor roster with country locations and a recent snapshot we can attach to the DPA. Please include whether any subprocessors have access to unredacted data paths.

3) If you have any evidence artifacts (last 12 months) showing region-only egress controls or SOC2/attestations scoped to regional controls, please include them.

Procurement looped in on cc — they’ll use the attachments for the DPA. If you can get the roster and a short note about transient egress behavior today, that will unblock the PO.

Appreciate it — we’re targeting a live rollout in EU production by Oct.

—Laura

Hi Laura —

Thanks — and great question. Short answers up front: yes, we support EU region pinning for account-scoped workloads; we also have a documented transient failover window for critical availability events. Details below + I attached a current subprocessor snapshot and a short note on transient behavior (see attachments).

What we’re attaching:
- Redwood_subprocessors_snapshot_20260808.csv (columns: vendor, service, role, country, access_scope)
- DPA-exception-escrow-notes.pdf (summary of transient egress scenarios and mitigations)
- DPA_FintechCo_redlines_Connor.pdf (starting point for the DPA with redlines)

Region pinning (how it works):
- Customer routing: requests for tenant-scoped data are routed to EU-only serving pools by policy.
- Storage/Logs: primary persisted data for EU tenants remains in EU regions.
- Transient failover: during an EU region outage we may temporarily route compute or analytics pipelines to adjacent region capacity to preserve availability. Any transient egress is limited to ephemeral KV/cache and is not persisted to long-term storage by default. We document the policy and max transient duration as follows: 72 hours for critical incident remediation unless otherwise agreed in writing (we can include a shorter SLA in the DPA if needed).

Subprocessor access: the CSV marks 'access_scope' for each subprocess; in short, the vast majority are limited to telemetry/infra (no access to application payloads). We’ll provide a redacted evidence bundle suitable for sharing with your legal/procurement teams. If procurement needs a full, signed subprocessor attestation, we can arrange a supplemental NDA and produce an unredacted roster for their review.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share the attachments (see above) and a one-page summary for procurement explaining the transient egress controls.
- If that’s still insufficient, Marissa can propose specific DPA wording or an SLA addendum for the failover window.
- Happy to jump on a 30m call with your legal/procurement this week.

Connor / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick reply and the files. A couple of procurement questions before we escalate to legal:

• We need confirmation in the DPA that any transient egress used for failover is purely ephemeral and will not result in long-term storage outside EU. Can you add explicit contractual language that non-persistent transient compute will not be used for analytics pipelines without customer consent?

• Can you provide the last quarterly snapshot of the subprocessor roster with timestamps for when each vendor was last assessed? The CSV is helpful but procurement requires an assessment date column.

• If you offer a limited SLA addendum that guarantees EU-only routing except for declared incidents (and a playbook for notification), that would speed sign-off.

We can sign the PO if these three items are addressed.

—Procurement (FintechCo)
procurement@fintech-co.com

[one-line reply from Laura: happy to coordinate legal review once we have the updated DPA + roster]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-12T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geofence waiver & subprocessor evidence

Hi all —

Thanks for the clear asks. I’ll own the DPA update and SLA addendum. Summary of commitments we can provide in writing for the DPA and pull-through into the contract:

1) EU region pinning: account and tenant routing will be documented as EU-only for production workloads.

2) Transient failover & non-persistence: we will add DPA language that any temporary routing to non-EU compute is limited to ephemeral compute/KV/cache, is not written to long-term storage, and is used only for availability remediation. We will add an explicit prohibition on using transient failover for batch analytics that write egressed data without customer consent.

3) Evidence and roster: Connor has attached the 2026-08-08 roster; we will re-run a quarterly extract that includes an "assessment_date" column and provide that CSV within 48 hours. If procurement requires an unredacted roster under an NDA, we will coordinate with your legal team for a controlled exchange.

4) SLA addendum & notification playbook: we will provide a short addendum guaranteeing EU-only routing except during declared incidents, with a notification playbook (outage classification, estimated window, and remediation steps). Defaults: declared incidents and temporary routing will be communicated to the customer within 2 hours of failover.

Action items (what we will deliver to you):
- Revised DPA PDF with explicit transient egress clause (Marissa) — target: 2026-08-14
- Updated subprocessor roster with assessment_date column (Connor) — target: 2026-08-14
- SLA addendum + notification playbook (Markus) — target: 2026-08-16
- DocuSign link for DPA signature once redlines are agreed (shared here): https://app.docusign.com/EXT/SigningStart?token=abc123def456

If that timeline works, please confirm and we’ll proceed. If you prefer legal-to-legal redline first, share your preferred collaborate link and we’ll have our counsel respond.

Best —
